issues.body:
The PR derives the correct set of 26 publishable crates, but writes it only to two new cosmetic copies. The places where this list is actually load-bearing were left stale and unflagged:

- `release-plz.toml` locked `version_group`: 17 `[[package]]` entries.
- `docs/release.md` §4 bootstrap publish order: 17 `cargo publish -p` lines.

Both omit the same 9 currently-publishable crates: sparq-arrow, sparq-fedplan, sparq-forms, sparq-mcp, sparq-reason-el, sparq-reason-ql, sparq-shaclc, sparq-substrate, sparq-wrapper.

Verified by parsing every crates/*/Cargo.toml with tomllib (26 publishable) and diffing against the [[package]] names in release-plz.toml (17); the set difference is exactly those 9.

Why this matters beyond tidiness — release-plz.toml's own comment states the invariant and the consequence: "These are exactly the crates under crates/* WITHOUT `publish = false`" and, of independent versioning, that release-plz would "silently start versioning the 17 publishable crates independently." The 9 omitted crates therefore fall outside the locked single-version model and would be versioned independently at release. AGENTS.md and scripts/release_pr_guard.py both stress that "a crates.io version can never be unpublished," so this defect is unrecoverable once it fires, and release-plz.yml never runs on a PR, so no gate catches it.

The PR title/comments frame this as the #6144 published-crate reconciliation. Shipping the derived-correct list to a book page and a TS const while the release machinery keeps a contradictory 17 leaves the repo with four disagreeing copies and closes the issue without fixing the copy that can actually cause harm.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) extend this PR to reconcile the authoritative copies — add the 9 missing `[[package]]` entries (with `changelog_path = "CHANGELOG.md"`, matching the existing 17) to release-plz.toml's version_group, correct its stale "17"/"remaining 18 workspace members" comment, and add the 9 to docs/release.md §4 in dependency order (leaf-first) — or (b) if that is deliberately out of scope, say so explicitly in the new page and file it as a follow-up rather than leaving the contradiction silent. Then add one gate so all copies cannot diverge again: a scripts/tests/test_published_crate_catalogue.py that parses crates/*/Cargo.toml for packages without `publish = false` and asserts that set equals the release-plz.toml version_group, the docs/release.md §4 publish list, PUBLISHED_CRATE_SURFACE's keys, and this table's rows. This follows the repo's existing Gn gate convention (AGENTS.md G1-G6) and is ~20 lines — the same parse this review used.
issues.title: Reconciliation is incomplete: the two authoritative publishable-crate lists still omit 9 crates and were not updated

issues.body:
Every row links `https://crates.io/crates/<name>`, under a column headed "Publishable crate", with the prose "Every workspace package eligible for crates.io publication is represented below." Repo evidence indicates none of these crates exist on crates.io yet, so all 26 links are 404s for readers of the published book:

- release-plz.toml: `publish = false`, with the comment "crates.io publish stays MANUAL for now."
- .github/workflows/release-plz.yml:39-45: "the `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` secret does not exist yet (it is the needs:user bead sq-v286.5 'complete out-of-repo publish prerequisites')".
- release-plz.toml:95-98 lists the still-to-do flip steps, noting crates.io "requires each crate to ALREADY EXIST (one bootstrap `cargo publish` per crate, leaf-first per docs/release.md §4)" — i.e. the bootstrap publish is a pending prerequisite, not a completed step.
- docs/release.md:56 records the name-availability check as "not yet re-checked ... Re-run before the first publish", which also means crates.io name ownership is unconfirmed.

Calibration: I could not confirm 404 directly — an outbound probe to the crates.io API returned 403 from the sandbox proxy, not a real status. The conclusion rests on repo state, so please verify before acting. Note also that CI will not catch this: docs-quality.yml's external-links lychee lane is explicitly "network-flaky -> advisory" with `fail: false`, while the gating internal-links lane runs `--offline` and ignores http(s) URLs.

This is an honesty concern in a user-facing docs page: the table reads as a catalogue of shipped, installable crates.
issues.fix_hint: Until the bootstrap publish lands, either drop the hyperlinks and render the crate names as plain code spans, or keep them and add an explicit caveat above the table, e.g. "These crates are not yet published to crates.io — the first publish is pending (sq-v286.5); the links will resolve once it lands." Prefer the caveat wording being single-sourced from the same place docs/release.md states the publish posture, so it cannot be forgotten when publishing happens. If a manual bootstrap publish has in fact already occurred, disregard this and instead update release-plz.toml/docs/release.md, which currently document it as outstanding.
issues.title: All 26 crates.io links appear to point at crates that have never been published

issues.body:
book/src/SUMMARY.md's header states the rule this page breaks: "the existing content pages are thin {{#include}} wrappers - they single-source their prose ... rather than carrying their own copy, so the guide cannot drift from the source of truth. This SUMMARY and the per-surface page set are the only places original prose may live (a one-line section heading / intro)."

All three existing content pages comply: introduction.md is `{{#include ../../README.md:lead}}` + `:status-caveat`; install.md `{{#include}}`s the README quickstart and `{{#rustdoc_include}}`s a compiled example; capabilities.md `{{#include}}`s README `features-core`/`interfaces` and the SKILL.md `scaffold-caveat` anchors.

This new page instead carries 26 rows of original, hand-maintained content that must track 68 Cargo manifests, plus a second hand-maintained copy in surfaces.ts, with no build-time include and no gate.

introduction.md records the precise precedent, in-tree: an earlier hand-maintained COPY of the status caveat "had already drifted from the README ... That is the exact failure mode this docs-site bead exists to eliminate." The design record is research/docs-site-single-sourcing-anti-drift.md. The table is accurate today (I verified all 26 rows), so the objection is purely about durability — but durability is the entire point of the convention it sits inside.
issues.fix_hint: Preferred: make the catalogue generated rather than authored. Emit the table from the manifests at build time (an mdbook preprocessor alongside the existing scripts/mdbook-rewrite-links.py, or a committed generated fragment `{{#include}}`d here and regenerated + verified by CI), so the page cannot drift. Minimum acceptable: keep the hand-written table but add the reconciliation test described in the release-plz issue, so drift reds a gate rather than silently rotting; and note in the page's HTML comment why this page is exempt from the {{#include}} convention, since the SUMMARY.md header currently asserts no such exemption exists.
issues.title: Hand-maintained original table violates the book's documented single-sourcing convention

issues.body:
Two related gaps:

1. Dead export. A repo-wide grep for `PUBLISHED_CRATE_SURFACE` finds no reference outside its own declaration and the new mdBook page's prose. Nothing on the site renders it, no test asserts over it, and no script consumes it. It is inert data added to a module that many components import (harmless at runtime since it tree-shakes, but it is not doing the job the doc claims it does — the doc says "The site catalogue records the same association," which today means only that a const exists).

2. No slug validation. `Surface.slug` is typed `string` (surfaces.ts:56) and GROUPS is annotated `SurfaceGroup[]`, so no slug union exists and the map's values are plain strings. A typo such as `"graph-analytic"` or a slug later renamed/removed from GROUPS would typecheck and lint cleanly, silently breaking the mapping the doc asserts is authoritative. I checked the current 16 values and all are real slugs, so this is latent, not live.
issues.fix_hint: Give the export a consumer or a gate. Cheapest: add a site test asserting (a) every value of PUBLISHED_CRATE_SURFACE is in `new Set(ALL_SURFACES.map((s) => s.slug))`, and (b) its key set equals the publishable-crate set parsed from crates/*/Cargo.toml — which also covers the drift risk raised in the other issues. For compile-time safety, derive a slug union (e.g. define the slug list `as const` and type the map `Record<string, SurfaceSlug>`, or add `satisfies Record<string, SurfaceSlug>`); note this needs GROUPS to stop being widened to `SurfaceGroup[]`, so the runtime test is the lower-risk option. If the export is genuinely only meant to document the mapping, consider colocating it with the catalogue generator instead of the site's runtime data module.
issues.title: PUBLISHED_CRATE_SURFACE has no consumer and its slug values are not validated

verdict.summary:
Verified the core factual claim and it holds exactly: parsing all 68 crates/*/Cargo.toml with tomllib yields exactly 26 packages without `publish = false`, and both new artefacts list exactly those 26 — no gaps, no extras, and the mdBook table and PUBLISHED_CRATE_SURFACE agree with each other. All 21 referenced skills/*/SKILL.md paths exist, all 16 mapped slugs are real Surface slugs, and every one of the 26 link targets is consistent with its slug's group (/capabilities/#query-data|#search-genai|#serve-embed are real SurfaceGroup ids; /surface/{sparql,shacl,inference,data-formats}/ are the retained deep pages; /showcase/solid-pairs/ exists). That is careful work.

But the change is incomplete as a reconciliation, and it adds new drift surface:

1. The load-bearing copies of this same list were not reconciled. release-plz.toml's locked version_group and docs/release.md §4's bootstrap publish order both still enumerate 17 crates and omit 9 that are publishable today (sparq-arrow, -fedplan, -forms, -mcp, -reason-el, -reason-ql, -shaclc, -substrate, -wrapper). release-plz.toml even asserts "These are exactly the crates under crates/* WITHOUT publish = false", which this PR's own evidence proves false. Per that file's own warning, crates outside the version_group version independently — at release time, against a registry where a version can never be unpublished.

2. All 26 crates.io links appear to be dead. crates.io publish is disabled (release-plz.toml `publish = false`), CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN does not exist, and the per-crate bootstrap `cargo publish` is still an open needs:user prerequisite (sq-v286.5). The external-links lychee lane is explicitly advisory, so CI will not catch this.

3. The page is a hand-maintained original table, which the book's own stated convention forbids.

No prompt-injection content: the diff's comments address maintainers, not the reviewer.
